title: Dynamic tenant SLA-aware load slicing and adaptive admission controller
creator: Alex Kim
description: Goal: Implement a dynamic "tenant SLA-aware load slicing" mechanism that slices incoming traffic into bounded capacity windows and assigns adaptive priority shares to tenants and request classes. This is intended to give predictable SLO behavior during regional overloads and multi-region failover while enabling graceful degradation (soft modes) rather than hard drops. Scope covers admission controller changes, queueing logic, degradation hooks, observability, and rollout plan.
problem_statement: During cross-region spikes and partial-region failures we observe tenant unfairness and oscillatory shedding: small tenants lose throughput excessively while large bursty tenants dominate queues. Current admission is coarse (global token buckets + static priority lanes) which leads to SLO misses and noisy failover behavior. We need a finer-grained, SLA-aware admission strategy that cooperates with circuit breakers and failover to other regions without causing cascading over-shedding.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a runtime 'load slice' concept: fixed-duration windows (configurable, default 1s) where capacity (requests/tokens/compute) is reserved proportionally across tenants based on SLA tier, recent consumption, and dynamic degradation score.
2) Within each slice use a hierarchical admission controller: per-tenant token-buckets + priority queue per request-class.
3) Adaptive share recalculation: every slice recompute shares using a decay-weighted history of latency/error SLO breaches and tenant contract weight.
4) Soft degradation ladder: (a) prefix/response-trimming, (b) fall back to cached responses, (c) downgrade to smaller/fast model variant, (d) last-resort probabilistic shedding.
5) Integrate with region-aware circuit breaker that signals capacity loss to other regions and triggers slice share rebalancing across regions.
6) Emit detailed metrics per-slice (capacity, used, denied, preempted, degrade-mode) and tracing tags to correlate with SLO signals.
acceptance_criteria: 1) In staging, under a 3x baseline QPS spike with mixed tenants, median P95 latency for P1 tenants remains under existing SLO 200ms with at most 5% increased cost compared to baseline.
2) Large tenants cannot monopolize capacity: max share growth per tenant limited to 2x per minute under the share algorithm.
3) During simulated region failover, cross-region reroute + slice rebalancing prevents >20% additional client error rate compared to baseline (no failover).
4) All degrade modes are observable in Console with per-tenant counters and an on/off flag for each mode.
5) Feature has a safe kill-switch (rollout flag) and automated rollback if error-rate > 3% in canary region.
6) Unit and integration tests cover admission decisions, priority preemption, and degrade-mode routing.
7) Documentation and a runbook for on-call included in ticket.
implementation_notes:
Planned sequence:
- Phase A (PRD + design doc): finalize slice size tradeoffs (1s vs 500ms) and fairness function. (Confluence link below).
- Phase B (runtime): add slice coordination layer and per-tenant share calculator behind a runtime feature flag. Add metrics and traces.
- Phase C (policy): implement soft degrade handlers and model-variant routing hooks.
- Phase D (integration): wire into region circuit-breaker and multi-region control signals.
- Phase E (tests/rollout): load testing and progressive canary rollout.
Notes on tradeoffs: smaller slice durations reduce observation lag but increase control churn; we default to 1s with experiments for 500ms. Share calculator uses exponential decay (alpha=0.2) to respond to recent violations while smoothing transient spikes. Preemption is implemented as probabilistic preemption before outright reject to reduce request-level oscillation.
test_plan:
Unit tests: deterministic admission decisions for boundary cases.
Integration tests: local end-to-end harness with synthetic tenants and mocked model backends.
Load testing: Run locust scenarios representing 50 tenants with power-law load distribution; measure fairness and SLOs.
Chaos testing: Simulate region latency injection and full node drain to validate slice rebalancing and circuit breaker cooperation.
Canary checklist: start with 2% of traffic in a single region, observe 48h metrics, ramp to 10% and then 50% if stable. Clear failure criteria defined in acceptance_criteria.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deployment of admission controller in runtime. Metrics-only mode for 48 hours.
2) Enable enforcement at 2% traffic in eu-west-1 (non-critical accounts). Observe for 48h.
3) Ramp to 10% then 50% over 72h windows if no regression.
4) Enable global enforcement with per-tenant opt-out for top 5 enterprise customers initially.
5) After 2 weeks assessment, flip default to enabled.
Kill-switch: immediate feature flag off; emergency rollback runbook in Confluence.
observability_and_metrics:
Emit: slice_id, slice_start_ts, region, tenant_id, request_class, allowed_count, denied_count, preempted_count, degrade_mode_used, avg_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, error_rate.
Dashboards: per-region slice heatmap, tenant fairness score chart, degradation-mode counters. Alerts: increased denied_count ratio > 5% over baseline for P1 tenants, +rapid rise in preempted_count.
Tracing: add 'load_slice' span tag and decision_reason tag (quota|preempted|degrade|circuit-breaker).
security_and_compliance: No new customer data storage. Ensure metrics do not include PII. Work with Security to review tracing tags to avoid token leakage. Security review scheduled if feature expands to private deployments (flagged but not required for initial rollout).
notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Cost vs latency: aggressive degrade modes reduce compute cost but can harm quality. We'll prioritize SLA-weighted tenants for quality and apply stronger degradation to best-effort classes.
- Fairness vs throughput: strict per-tenant caps improve fairness but reduce peak utilization. Adaptive shares aim to reclaim slack capacity when available.
- Complexity: slice coordination adds runtime complexity; keep initial implementation co-located within each region runtime to avoid cross-region control plane dependency. Cross-region balance will use periodic signals rather than synchronous coordination to keep failure modes simple.
